On 2023-03-06, the user asked the assistant to act as a startup lead product manager and write a product requirements document (PRD) from a specification for StressXpress, dated 2022-11-08, version 1. StressXpress is intended to help employers monitor employee stress, identify burnout early, and reduce the costs of staff replacement and onboarding.

The StressXpress specification describes three employee background questionnaires, analyzed by the server to produce an onboarding report and a red/amber/green triage status: red means “Burnout,” amber means “Stressed,” and green means “Acceptable.” Employers receive reports too. The specification calls for follow-up checks at green: “30 periods” (unit unclear in the source), amber: every 14 days, and red: every 7 days. Follow-ups use facial-change and voice-algorithm analysis; red status replaces those checks with a gamified dexterity task combining button use and voice control. If status returns to amber, facial and voice checks resume.

In the StressXpress specification, employers upload employee details, control which employees are actively managed, issue login identifiers and passwords, and are billed monthly according to the number of active employees. The employee identifier may be a nonfunctional email-like address, provided its domain matches the hosting company (example: ID1940@company.com); the server does not send email. Employees submit the identifier and password to the server for REST validation. On successful validation, the server returns menu links, including questionnaire and report options.

The StressXpress specification assigns the server responsibility for generating psychological questions, analyzing responses, determining triage colors, and storing and managing historical data. It says an employee moving to another participating employer can continue with their existing personal history through new employer credentials linked to that data. Employers are to have broad SQL-based data-analysis access; employees can access previously defined reports through the mobile-app menu.

On 2023-03-06, the assistant drafted a PRD titled “Product Requirement Document” for StressXpress, version 1.0, with release date November 8, 2022. The draft organized the source material into overview, mobile-app concept, employer responsibilities, employee mobile device, server responsibilities, and gamification sections. It described the document as a rough draft subject to updates during development.

records.text: When asked for nearby sandwich places, the assistant suggested Social Bite, Rocket Cafe, Oink, The Pastry Section, and Pep & Fodder. The assistant described Oink as known for hog roast sandwiches.
